text: Raw rows are landing safely in staging. This video builds the middle third of the pipeline: Transform — cleaning raw text into real types, and resolving each row's store and product into the warehouse's surrogate keys.

First, a Data Conversion step casts every raw string to its real type — dates, decimals, integers. Its error output redirects to load_errors instead of failing the component, same as Extract. One bad price field shouldn't block the whole file.

A Derived Column then calculates net_sales_amount using the exact formula from the requirements brief — gross minus returns minus employee discount — the same formula enforced as a check constraint on the warehouse table, so SSIS and the database are guaranteed to agree.

Key resolution is two Lookups in sequence — store_id against dim_store, SKU against the current row of dim_product. Both are configured to redirect no-match rows to their own output, never ignore, never fail the whole component.

That matters enormously. A SKU that doesn't resolve yet is a real, recurring case — a new product sold before the catalog caught up — and it needs a visible landing spot, not a silent drop and not a blank key.

Rows that pass both lookups land in a clean table shaped exactly like fact_sales, still inside staging — what Load reads from next. The stage logs both its success count and its no-match counts, visible even on a night that otherwise reports success.

Get that Lookup configuration even slightly wrong, and you get a package that reports success while quietly losing real data — exactly the bug we chase down several videos from now. Next: Load, and the logic that makes a retry safe.
